claim: Kandyan defensive capacity relied in part on difficult mountain terrain and controlled topographic knowledge, which constrained British military projection before 1815.
bounded_by: This supports terrain and guarded geographic knowledge as defensive mechanisms. It does not establish the stronger proposition that forests, passes, roads and bridges were deliberately left undeveloped as a formal statewide doctrine.
notes: Hard ceiling B until a Kandyan-era or colonial-era documentary anchor directly establishes deliberate non-development policy.
